survey: Image 5 is a gold five-pointed sheriff's star badge, floating against a purple sunburst background, tilted about 15–20° clockwise and turned slightly away from the camera. Main parts: (1) A star body with bevelled ridges running from each tip to the centre, and a raised rim along the edges. (2) Five gold balls, one on each tip. Each ball sits on a short neck at its point and joins the star cleanly; none floats or passes through the body. (3) A round raised boss in the centre holding a domed red stone, set flush in a gold ring. There is no pin or clasp on the back, which is fine for a front view. The object is meant to float as an icon, so there are no support problems. The ball count matches the point count (5 and 5). Nothing loose, hinged or load-bearing could fail.

errors.where: Star arms, especially the bottom-left arm compared with the top and bottom-right arms
errors.what: The five points are not even. The bottom-left arm is short and wide, while the top and bottom-right arms are long and thin. The inner corners sit at uneven distances from the centre, and the tilt alone does not explain the difference. A stamped sheriff's star is a regular star, so the badge looks slightly warped.

The domed red stone in the centre is an invented part. Real sheriff's stars have a stamped or engraved centre (a seal, emblem or the word 'SHERIFF'), not a gemstone. Game art accepts it as a stylisation, but it is not true to the object.

fix: A regular, symmetrical five-pointed sheriff's star badge: all five arms the same length and width, inner corners evenly spaced around the centre, and a round gold ball on each tip. In the centre, a raised round gold boss with a simple stamped emblem or engraved ring instead of a red gemstone.
